This video is about "AMUL 🐄 The Revolution That Saved Millions of Farmers | Case Study | White Revolution | Live Hindi"

In this in-depth video, we explore the Amul success story, a tale of innovation, resilience, and empowerment that revolutionized India’s dairy industry and transformed it into the world’s largest milk producer. This is the inspiring journey of Dr. Verghese Kurien, hailed as the Father of the White Revolution, and Tribhuvandas Patel, who laid the foundation for Amul's cooperative model to uplift the Farmers of Gujarat.

How It All Began
Amul’s story began in 1946 when farmers in Gujarat were exploited by middlemen and faced unfair practices. Tribhuvandas Patel, a visionary leader, united these farmers to establish a cooperative, creating the Kaira District Cooperative Milk Producers Union Ltd., famously known as Amul. But the journey wasn’t easy. In 1949, Dr. Verghese Kurien, an engineering graduate, joined the cooperative and introduced groundbreaking ideas to revolutionize the dairy sector. Together, Patel and Kurien empowered 36 lakh farmers, providing them with a sustainable livelihood and hope for a better future.

The White Revolution and Operation Flood
Dr. Kurien spearheaded Operation Flood, the largest dairy development program in the world. This initiative not only made India self-sufficient in milk production but also turned it into the largest producer globally. This video sheds light on How Amul Saved India from milk shortages and laid the foundation for rural development, women’s empowerment, and economic independence.

Marketing Genius and the Amul Girl
Amul’s success is not just about milk; it’s also about branding. The genius of Sylvester daCunha, the creator of the iconic Amul Girl, brought a fresh and witty perspective to advertising. These advertisements became a cultural phenomenon, resonating with every Indian household and ensuring Amul’s dominance in the market.

How Amul Killed Competition
Through innovation, fair pricing, and a farmer-first approach, Amul outperformed its competitors, many of whom were multinational giants. This AMUL Case Study demonstrates how the cooperative model can thrive in a competitive landscape, ensuring quality products while supporting its backbone—the farmers.
